fixes.explanation: Joel describes the reverse. Behind this army the land is like a desert wasteland. It is like the Garden of Eden in front of them, before the fire and flame get there. A field ready to pick would be a nice thought, friend, but it isn't what the verse says.

No water shows up in this verse, baker. Joel talks about fire devouring in front and flame scorching behind. Behind them, the land is like a desert wasteland. Dry as a cookie sheet left in the oven all night.
That's not what Joel describes. The nations writhe in horror, and every face turns pale. He doesn't say anyone rushes out to fight. I think I'd be stuck in place too, on my gold base.
That's the one. Joel says "They do not jostle one another; each proceeds in his path." He compares them to mighty men and men of war, and each one keeps to his own path. Not a step out of place.
You got it, baker. Joel says they climb into houses "…entering through windows like thieves." Windows are how this army gets in. That's the way they come.
Joel says it differently. They climb into houses, entering through windows like thieves. Front doors aren't how the verse has them coming in, friend. It's windows.
Right, baker. Joel says "The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars lose their brightness." Sun, moon and stars all lose their light. That's a sky I wouldn't want to look at.

Pharaoh, the king of Egypt (Exodus 5:1), isn't in this passage at all. Joel says the one who raises His voice is the LORD, in the presence of His army. So this voice isn't coming from any earthly throne. It's His.
Right, baker. Joel says "…consecrate a fast, proclaim a sacred assembly." The horn is calling for people to come together before the LORD. It's the ram's horn from verse 1, with a different job.
Nobody is sent to the walls in this verse. Joel says to consecrate a fast and proclaim a sacred assembly. The call is to gather the people, not to post lookouts.

Joel never tells the priests to ask for a king. The words he gives them begin "Spare Your people, O LORD…" They also ask Him not to make His heritage a reproach, an object of scorn among the nations. A king doesn't come up, friend.

Nothing about their numbers shows up in the priests' words. The question they ask the LORD to head off is "Where is their God?" That's the one the nations might ask. I don't know about you, friend, but I think that one would sting.
